generatedProse.practice-connection:
Everything in this course connects to work you are already doing. Across your studies you reflect, or fail to reflect, after most tasks: an assignment returned with feedback, a presentation that did not land, a project that overran. The students whose work improves are the ones who reflect on those experiences with structure and act on what they find, rather than moving straight on to the next task. Read what follows as being about your own assignments and feedback, not reflection in the abstract.

The same habit matters once you graduate. In any role you are given work, judged against a standard, and asked to do better next time, and the people who improve are the ones who reflect deliberately and change something as a result. Building the habit of structured reflection now is one you keep for the rest of your working life.
